title: Grade 6 French — Wed, May 27
description: Les adjectifs possessifs (Possessive Adjectives) — Day 3 of 5
subject: french

questions.question: How do you say 'my brother' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Mon frère' = my brother. 'Frère' is masculine → use 'mon' (my, masculine singular). Mon/Ma/Mes = my.

questions.question: How do you say 'my sister'?
questions.explanation: 'Ma sœur' = my sister. 'Sœur' is feminine → use 'ma' (my, feminine singular).

questions.question: How do you say 'my parents'?
questions.explanation: 'Mes parents' = my parents. 'Parents' is plural → use 'mes' (my, plural — same for masculine and feminine).

questions.question: What is the rule for using 'mon' instead of 'ma' before a feminine noun?
options: Use mon before feminine nouns starting with a vowel or silent h
Use mon when noun is plural
questions.explanation: Before feminine nouns starting with a vowel sound: 'mon amie' (not 'ma amie'), 'mon école' (not 'ma école'). This is for ease of pronunciation.

questions.question: How do you say 'your (informal) father'?
questions.explanation: 'Ton père' = your (informal) father. 'Père' is masculine → 'ton'. Ton/Ta/Tes = your (informal, singular).

questions.question: How do you say 'his/her mother'?
questions.explanation: 'Sa mère' = his/her mother. 'Mère' is feminine → 'sa'. Son/Sa/Ses = his/her/its. Note: French doesn't distinguish 'his' from 'her' — gender of the NOUN matters, not the owner.

questions.question: What does 'son ami' mean? (it is ambiguous — why?)
options: his or her friend (m) — French does not distinguish
questions.explanation: 'Son ami' can mean 'his friend' OR 'her friend' — French possessives agree with the noun gender, not the owner's gender. Context tells us whose friend.

questions.question: How do you say 'our family'?
questions.explanation: 'Notre famille' = our family. Notre/Nos = our. Singular: 'notre', Plural: 'nos'. 'Famille' is singular → 'notre'.

questions.question: How do you say 'your (formal/plural) children'?
questions.explanation: 'Vos enfants' = your (formal/plural) children. 'Vos' is plural form of 'votre'. Votre/Vos = your (formal or plural).

questions.question: How do you say 'their house'?
questions.explanation: 'Leur maison' = their house. 'Leur/Leurs' = their. Singular noun → 'leur'. Plural noun → 'leurs'.

questions.question: Complete: 'J'aime ___ école.' (my school — école starts with a vowel)
questions.explanation: 'Mon école' — even though 'école' is feminine, we use 'mon' before it because it starts with a vowel. This avoids the clash of two vowel sounds.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly says 'She loves her brother'?
questions.explanation: 'Son frère' = her brother. 'Frère' is masculine → 'son'. Remember: French possessives agree with the NOUN (frère = masculine), not with 'she'.

questions.question: Translate: 'Our grandparents live in Jaipur.'
questions.explanation: 'Nos grands-parents' (plural → 'nos'). 'Habiter à' = to live in. 'Nos grands-parents habitent à Jaipur.'

questions.question: What is WRONG in this sentence: 'Mon sœur est gentille.'?
options: 'Mon' should be 'Ma' — sœur is feminine and doesn't start with a vowel
questions.explanation: 'Sœur' is feminine and starts with a consonant → use 'ma', not 'mon'. Correct: 'Ma sœur est gentille.'

questions.question: Complete the table: mon/ma/mes = my; ton/ta/tes = your; son/sa/ses = his/her; ___/___ = our:
questions.explanation: Notre (singular) / Nos (plural) = our. Votre/Vos = your (formal/plural). Leur/Leurs = their.
